memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So they went up out of Egypt and came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan. They told him, 'Joseph is still alive! In fact, he is ruler of all Egypt.' Jacob was stunned; he did not believe them." — Gen 45:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Jacob was stunned; he did not believe them." The Hebrew is vivid — his heart went numb. The news is too big. He has grieved this son for over twenty years, and grief that old has hardened into a settled certainty. Joseph is dead. That is the fixed fact of his life.

And now they are telling him it is not true.

Sometimes good news is harder to believe than bad news. When you have made peace with a loss, hope feels dangerous. To believe again is to risk being devastated again.

Do not judge Jacob for this. Remember that when the women came from the empty tomb, the disciples thought their words were nonsense and did not believe them (Lk 24:11). Resurrection news is genuinely hard to take in. It is not that faith is easy and doubt is shameful — the God we serve does things so far beyond our experience that our first honest reaction is often numbness.

But notice: Jacob's unbelief did not make it untrue. Joseph was alive whether his father believed it or not. Truth does not wait for our feelings to catch up.

If your heart feels numb to good news today, be patient with yourself. God is patient with you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there good news from God you have found hard to actually believe?
2. Has old grief made hope feel dangerous to you?
3. What helps your heart catch up with what you know to be true?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, sometimes Your goodness is bigger than my heart can take in. Be patient with my numbness, and help my faith catch up with the truth. Amen.
